<h2>"Paid version" of Google local businesses</h2>
<p>Google My Business has launched a paid membership model. Currently, only a few types of merchants in a few areas have received invitations. The price is US$50 a month. Merchants that have applied and been approved will have a Google Guaranteed green check on the information bar. When consumers are dissatisfied, they can file a claim with Google.</p>

<div class="wp-block-group" id="toc-2"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2>Referrer policy update after Chrome v85</h2>
<p>Chrome's default referrer policy will be changed from the original<code><em>no-referrer-when-downgrade</em></code>changed to<em><code>strict-origin-when-cross-origin</code></em>. This does not have any direct impact on SEO. It is mainly due to stricter regulations on information security. Advertisers may lose important information (ex: which pages the user viewed), but the impact on general websites may be that the Full Referral in GA will have less information.</p>
<p>Google Search will not tell you the search terms of natural traffic, also because there are<code><em>Referrer Policy: origin</em></code>(regardless of whether the next page is the same origin or not, it refers to the origin information), so the URL contains keyword parameters (<em>?q=digital engine</em>) is stuck.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 13 – 2020.07.16~2020.07.31" decoding="async" loading="lazy" src="https://www.maxlist.xyz/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/Chrome-85-Referer-Policy-%E6%9B%B4%E6%96%B0_Max%E8%A1%8C%E9%8A%B7%E8%AA%8C.jpg"/><figcaption><a href="https://www.maxlist.xyz/2020/08/03/chrome-85-referer-policy/?utm_source=google&amp;utm_medium=internal&amp;utm_campaign=max-is-awesome">[Chrome 85 update] A brief discussion of Referer-Policy and update impact</a>by MAX Marketing Journal</figcaption></figure>
<p>For information about Referrer Policy and more changes, please refer to the above article, which has a very detailed explanation. It is recommended that everyone who is studying SEO can try to understand it. It may not be directly related to SEO, but after understanding it, you will have a clearer understanding of the entire Internet ecosystem!</p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>
<div class="wp-block-group" id="toc-3"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2>Bing webmaster tools overhaul completed</h2>
<p>In February this year, Bing announced that it would revamp its webmaster tools, which was finally completed at the end of July. As previously introduced in previous newsletters, several new features include:<em>URL submission tool, URL removal tool, crawl limit, website health diagnosis, backlinks, URL submission</em>...etc.</p>
<p>If you missed it, you can check out previous issues of the newsletter or read the official announcement. Regarding the whole topic, I think this revision is quite sincere. Although the traffic from most websites from Bing is not mainstream, many tools provide functions that Google Search Console does not have, and authentication is very convenient. I recommend everyone to check it out and play around.</p>

<h2>GSC filter adds "News" category</h2>
<p>The filters in Google Webmaster Tools have added a fourth "<em>News(News)</em>" category, the original three categories are "<em>Network (Web)</em>」「<em>picture(Image)</em>」「<em>Video(Video)</em>」。</p>
<p>It is worth noting that the "News" category refers specifically to search results for news (<a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=%E5%8F%B0%E7%81%A3&amp;tbm=nws">tbm=nws</a>) instead of top news in general search results.</p>

<h2>Two changes in lazy loading of Chrome</h2>
<p>These two updates are related to web perdormance and can save unnecessary data traffic consumption. Lazy-Loading, which is natively supported by the browser, will not have any negative impact on SEO. It is quite simple to install and can be used with confidence.</p>
<p>First, Chrome will support iframe lazy-loading, in the same way as images, just put it in &lt;iframe&gt;<code>loading="lazy"</code>is enough</p>
<figure class="wp-block-video"><video controls="" playsinline="" preload="metadata" src="https://storage.googleapis.com/web-dev-assets/iframe-lazy-loading/lazyload-iframes-compressed.webm"></video><figcaption>lazy-loading iframe example</figcaption></figure>
<p>Secondly, the lazy loading distance of the picture will be determined by<code>3000px</code>changed to<code>1250px</code>(4G) or<code>2500px</code>(3G)。</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large is-resized"><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 13 – 2020.07.16~2020.07.31" class="wp-image-1592" decoding="async" height="270" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/08/%E5%9C%96%E7%89%87lazy-loading%E8%B7%9D%E9%9B%A2-1024x588.png" width="471"/><figcaption>image lazy-loading distance update</figcaption></figure>

<div class="wp-block-group" id="toc-9"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2>Google’s information at the antitrust public hearing</h2>
<p>I believe everyone has heard about this antitrust public hearing between the U.S. Congress and the four technology giants. There are quite a few reports in Chinese, so I won’t go into details here. Among them, I think there are two points that SEO practitioners may be more interested in. The following is the author’s understanding. You can take a look for reference.</p>
<h3 class="has-medium-font-size">(1.) Is Click a ranking factor?</h3>
<p>The answer is Yes, but it is a very indirect factor. It is not that as long as a certain web page has a lot of clicks on the search results, the ranking will gradually improve; the real operating mechanism is that Google will take back the click data on the SERP and feed it to the algorithm, and rely on machine learning to systematically optimize the results spit out by the overall algorithm. somewhat similar to them<a href="./seo-newsletter-issue-12.html#toc-8">How to deal with spam</a>, instead of manually reviewing and making changes one by one when someone reports it, this information is used as input to train its spam detection algorithms.</p>
<h3 class="has-medium-font-size">(2.) Look at Search from Google’s perspective</h3>
<p>A considerable part of this review document is Google’s internal discussion on how to maintain the status of its search engine. Most people may only understand “search engine” as services such as Bing, Yahoo, and Google. However, in Google’s own eyes, in addition to maintaining the status of the former (horizontal search engines), they do not want their status to be replaced by vertical search engines (vertical search engines) such as Amazon, YouTube, and Facebook.</p>
<p>link:<a href="https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/july-2020/Announcing-the-new-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-(migration-complete)">Inside report</a> / <a href="https://www.businessweekly.com.tw/international/blog/3003341">Business Weekly Report</a> / <a href="https://judiciary.house.gov/online-platforms-and-market-power/">US Congressional Review Documents</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>

<h2>Mobile version content priority indexing extended to March 2021</h2>
<p><a aria-label="undefined (opens in a new tab)" href="./seo-newsletter-issue-4.html#toc-1" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank">The fourth issue of e-newsletter</a>introduced that Google announced that it will implement mobile content-first indexing (Mobile First Indexing) for all websites in 2020.09. Due to the epidemic, Google decided to postpone this plan to March 2021 in order to give websites that have not yet been optimized for mobile versions more time to improve.</p>

<div class="wp-block-group" id="toc-12"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2>SEO Mythbusters: Website Speed (Page Speed)</h2>
<p>This episode’s myth buster, Martin invites Eric Enge (co-author of The Art of SEO) to discuss myths about website speed. It is mentioned that although website speed has an impact, content is the most important part. Improving a website's Lighthouse score from 90 to 95 will probably not result in a significant ranking improvement.</p>
<p>Speed ​​is important, but Google hopes that everyone will focus on "slow" or "normal" web pages. If the website speed is already fast enough, pursuing faster or faster will improve the user experience, but it will not have much advantage from an SEO perspective.</p>

<div class="wp-block-group" id="toc-13"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2>official video: Do special types of files need to be blocked in robots.txt?</h2>
<p>In this newbie video, John Mueller is asked "<em>Should I block special files like CSS, php.ini, or htaccess in robots.txt?</em>」</p>
<p>The short answer is NO! Files that will not be crawled do not need to be specifically declared in robots.txt. In addition, files such as CSS and JS that may be used to render web pages are not recommended to block Googltbot even if the text content on the web page is not changed.</p>
